structured_output.hypothesis: If Arizona's climate over the last 500 years fluctuated with a regular period of almost exactly 150 years, then century-smoothed ring-width chronologies of Arizona ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa) will show a statistically significant spectral peak at 140-160 years, and that peak will be the dominant low-frequency peak.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Use all ITRDB Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronologies that cover at least 1500-1980 AD. Build a regional mean chronology and analyse each site chronology as well. Apply a 100-year smoothing filter, then estimate the spectrum with multitaper or Blackman-Tukey. PASS if (a) the regional-mean spectrum has its highest peak at periods between 50 and 250 years inside 140-160 years, (b) that peak exceeds the 95% confidence limit of an AR(1) red-noise null (1000 Monte Carlo surrogates), and (c) at least 60% of the individual site chronologies show a significant peak (above the 95% red-noise limit) within 140-160 years.
structured_output.fail_criterion: FAIL if the regional-mean peak at 140-160 years does not exceed the 95% red-noise limit. FAIL if the dominant peak at periods of 50-250 years lies outside 135-165 years. FAIL if fewer than 40% of site chronologies show a significant peak within 140-160 years. Results between these bounds are reported as inconclusive and count as not confirming the claim.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson relies on A. E. Douglass's Arizona yellow-pine (Pinus ponderosa) ring-width series, smoothed with a century-long running mean. 'Regular periodicity of almost precisely 150 years' is read as a narrow spectral peak at 150 +/- 10 years that is statistically distinguishable from red noise. 'Climate' is read as the common ring-width signal, which is mainly moisture. The test does not separate moisture from temperature, because the data have no separate climate variable, so it does not assess the 'mainly moisture' qualifier. Modern reinterpretation: use ITRDB ring-width measurements detrended conservatively (negative-exponential or linear fit), because flexible standardization can remove low-frequency variance. 500 years contains only about 3.3 cycles of 150 years, so spectral resolution is poor. The 140-160 year band and the red-noise null account for this.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
dataset.why_it_fits: The ITRDB is the public archive of tree-ring measurements and chronologies, including Arizona Pinus ponderosa sites, the species Douglass used. Fields to use: species code PIPO, state or location (Arizona), the .rwl raw ring-width series and .crn chronologies, and year coverage. The data are filtered to sites spanning 1500-1980 AD, and the annual series are smoothed with a 100-year filter and analysed spectrally.
